entities.summary: Ivan Shishman of Bulgaria ruled as emperor (tsar) of Bulgaria in Tarnovo from 1371 to 3 June 1395. The authority of Ivan Shishman was limited to the central parts of the Bulgarian Empire. Ivan Shishman played a crucial role in the Bulgarian resistance against the Ottoman Empire, which had been expanding its territories in the Balkans since the late 14th century. The Ottoman conquest of Bulgaria in 1396 marked the beginning of a period of Ottoman dominance in the region. Despite his efforts, Ivan Shishman was unable to prevent the Ottoman Empire from conquering the Bulgarian capital of Tarnovo in 1396. Ivan Shishman's reign was marked by a series of conflicts with the Ottoman Empire, including the Battle of Nikopol in 1396, which was a major defeat for the Bulgarians. Ivan Shishman died on 11 June 1395, and his legacy was largely forgotten until the 19th century, when Bulgarian nationalism revived and the country's independence was sought.
